questions.prompt: What is the difference between `git add .` and `git add -A`?
options: `git add .` stages the current directory and below; `git add -A` stages all changes in the repo
questions.explanation: `git add .` stages changes in the current directory and below; `git add -A` stages all changes in the whole repository.

questions.prompt: What happens when you run `git commit` without `-m`?
options: Git opens your editor for the message
Git uses the last message again
Git commits with an empty message
questions.explanation: `-m` writes the message inline; without it, Git opens the configured editor so you can write the message.
`git restore --staged <file>` only unstages; `git restore <file>` discards the working-tree changes.
